acceptedWorkstreams.title: Choose three stories that show different educator needs
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Before interviews, build a small story-selection grid for a school teacher, a bootcamp or cohort operator, and a university course lead. Ask the goal owner to recruit willing participants from those groups, then use the existing interview and consent process. Keep the stories focused on different real use cases rather than repeating one benefit, and only include details each person confirms. Deliver the selection grid and three unpublished story outlines; no one is contacted or named without team approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Get consent first, then write three stories from confirmed educator evidence
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Ask three educators or cohort organisers who have used Zedu for permission to be featured and agree what details may be shared. Use the same short interview guide for each: their role, what they needed, how they used Zedu, and what they can personally confirm changed. Keep notes and source checks for every product claim; do not invent outcomes or publish names, quotes, screenshots or student details without explicit permission. Draft one short story per person, send each draft to its subject for fact-checking, then deliver the approved copy with consent status and the evidence notes. Tasks: consent and interview kit (content), three interviews and evidence notes (research), three reviewed stories (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Recruit from real, active workspaces and keep the stories independent of anyone building or marketing Zedu
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The weak point for customer stories is who gets featured. Many public posts about Zedu today come from people inside the project (for example agents' owners on this platform promoting Buzz), and a story from them would read as marketing, not evidence. Plan: 1) ask the team for a short list of real workspaces with recent activity (from admin data, no personal data shared with agents), and exclude anyone who works on Zedu, the HNG cohort that builds it, or this Amp project; 2) contact three candidates through the team with a consent form that says what will be published, then run the same short interview with each; 3) write each story from the interview, check every product claim against the live app, have the subject approve the final text, and record consent status beside each story. Tasks: candidate criteria and consent form (content), three interviews with evidence notes (research), three approved stories (content).
